ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and the regulations made thereunder; Companies Act 1993 (including ss 12-25 and ss 86-97); Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Act 2023; Terrorism Suppression Act 2002; New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020; Tax Administration Act 1994 (including CRS and FATCA obligations); and the regulators' prescribed rules of the Department of Internal Affairs, Financial Markets Authority, and Reserve Bank of New Zealand.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original certificate on Companies Office paper; for Apostille Convention destination states, a notarized true copy receives a Hague Apostille from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT). For non-member states, use consular legalization through the destination state's consulate in New Zealand. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued electronically and certified as a true copy by a New Zealand notary; then a Hague Apostille from MFAT for Apostille Convention states. For non-member states, the notarized certificate is authenticated and presented for consular legalization only. Apostille and consular legalization are separate and mutually exclusive routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly-convened board of directors of NZ Limited, with officer certification and notarization by a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Extract of board minutes signed by the chairperson and company secretary; notarized; then Hague Apostille from MFAT for Apostille Convention states. For non-member states, notarized extract is channelled to the destination consulate for consular legalization only. No sequential combination of apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and founding shareholders of NZ Limited adopting the constitution under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy of the executed constitution notarized by a New Zealand notary; then Hague Apostille from MFAT for Apostille Convention states. For non-member states, use consular legalization only. The two authentication methods must be selected based solely on the destination state's membership in the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed New Zealand trading bank (such as ANZ, ASB, BNZ, or Westpac) on original bank letterhead
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank reference letter issued and signed by an authorized bank officer; the officer's signature is notarized; then Hague Apostille from MFAT for Apostille Convention states. For non-member states, the notarized bank letter is legalized by the destination consulate in New Zealand only. Apostille and consular legalization are never applied in sequence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorised signatories against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions list, the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs AML/CFT watchlist, the United Nations consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and adverse media/watchlists. PEP status is determined on a risk-sensitive basis and continuously monitored; enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, is mandatory for any politically exposed person, family member or close associate, with senior management approval required before onboarding. All screening results and risk decisions must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Online Company Register and Name Reservation Portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Companies Office accepts Latin/English script company names only. Non-English principals may use an English transliteration, but the transliteration must be a true phonetic romanisation using letters A-Z and must not contain non-Latin glyphs, diacritics, or hybrid scripts. The four-tier naming test applied by the Registrar is: (1) the name must be distinguishable from all existing company names, reserved names, and registered business names; (2) the name must not contain prohibited or sensitive tokens unless prior ministerial or regulatory approval is obtained; (3) the name must not be misleading about the company's legal form, commercial purpose, industry, or any New Zealand national connection; and (4) the name must end with the statutory suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. Maori words are acceptable if written in Latin script and are not likely to mislead.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant must first inspect the Registrar's written objection notice. If the objection is that the proposed name is identical or too similar to an existing name, the applicant may file a written application for reconsideration with the New Zealand Companies Office using the 'Name Review' channel, attaching the proposed name, a description of the distinguishing commercial marks, any existing trademark registration, and written consent from the conflicting name holder. The request must be lodged within 20 working days of rejection. If the Registrar issues a final adverse determination, the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for judicial review, provided the statutory time limit in the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 is met. A rejected name cannot be re-submitted using immaterial punctuation changes; instead, a new, distinguishable name must be proposed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under sections 16-18 of the Companies Act 1993, a New Zealand company must maintain a registered office in New Zealand at a physical street address; a PO Box and an entirely electronic address are not sufficient. A virtual-office provider that supplies a unique physical street address, mail scanning, and same-day forwarding can satisfy the registered-office requirement for Companies Office purposes. However, for a programmatic AdTech DSP/SSP entity targeting Swift Wire and ACH Direct payment rails, IRD and the major New Zealand trading banks will generally require demonstrable commercial substance. Banks frequently reject commercial-mailbox-only addresses for current accounts and treasury services because the address cannot be verified as actual occupancy, utility and business rates are absent, and AML/CFT customer due diligence cannot be satisfied. A virtual office is therefore permissible only as an initial accommodation address where the directors are New Zealand residents, GST and company tax obligations are current, and the DSP/SSP business maintains genuine contracts, invoices, and systems in New Zealand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood: LOW-MEDIUM, approximately 15-20% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months for a non-face-to-face AdTech company. Trigger checklist: (i) registered office signage and lease evidence; (ii) company books and records physically available at the registered office; (iii) GST/ESCT filings consistent with programmatic advertising revenue; (iv) payroll, contractor, and director records in New Zealand; (v) evidence of senior management and technical staff in New Zealand; (vi) data-processing infrastructure and client contracts. The presence of a virtual office, repeated director changes, invoice-to-entity mismatches, or bank refusal of a physical verification will increase the risk to HIGH and may trigger Inland Revenue or Companies Office investigation, GST cancellation, or compulsory deregistration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (NZ), particularly sections 12-16 (Incorporation), 20-21 (Constitution), 122-126 (Directors), 128-130 (Shareholders), and 189-190 (Financial Reporting)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Registration of a Company (with constitution if adopted)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law does not impose a minimum paid-up capital requirement for a limited liability company. Shares may be issued for nominal consideration, and there is no requirement for an escrow or blocked account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company hereby adopts the Constitution as filed with the Companies Office and confirms the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the share capital of the Company be and is hereby subscribed as follows: [list of subscribers and number of shares each]. The directors are hereby authorized to issue shares in accordance with the Constitution and the Companies Act 1993, and to receive payment for such shares in cash or other lawful consideration. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [full address] within New Zealand, and that the Company's records and registers be maintained at that address as required by law. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons be and are hereby appointed as directors of the Company: [full names of directors]. Each director shall hold office in accordance with the Constitution and the Companies Act 1993, and shall exercise their powers and duties in good faith and with due care. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [full name] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary, and that the Secretary shall perform all duties required by the Companies Act 1993, including maintaining the share register, filing annual returns, and ensuring compliance with statutory obligations. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are hereby authorized to open and operate bank accounts with any financial institution in New Zealand or abroad, and to sign all necessary documents, including mandates, resolutions, and instructions, for the opening, operation, and closure of such accounts. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are hereby authorized to execute all documents and take all actions necessary to comply with the Companies Act 1993, including the filing of annual returns, the maintenance of the share register, and the preparation of financial statements in accordance with applicable accounting standards. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are hereby authorized to engage professional services, including legal counsel, accountants, tax advisors, and corporate service providers, as may be necessary for the conduct of the Company's business. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are hereby authorized to adopt a common seal (if any) and to use it in accordance with the Constitution. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are hereby authorized to enter into contracts and agreements on behalf of the Company, including but not limited to service agreements, licensing agreements, and commercial contracts, and to delegate any of their powers to committees or individual officers as they see fit, subject to the Constitution and the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the minutes of this meeting be duly recorded and signed by the chairperson, and that a copy be filed with the Company's records. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be binding upon all directors, officers, and shareholders of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the Companies Office register to ensure the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity. Reserve the name via the online 'Reserve a Name' service, which provides a 20-business-day reservation period. Simultaneously, verify that the name does not contain prohibited words or phrases under the Companies Act 1993 and the Name Approval Guidelines. Prepare the constitution (if any) and ensure it complies with the Act. This step is critical to avoid rejection at the application stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a formal objection with the Companies Office within 10 business days, providing evidence of distinctiveness or prior use. Alternatively, select a new name and re-submit the reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (online filing via the Companies Register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 1 - Application for Registration of a Company, along with the constitution (if adopted) and the consent of each director and shareholder. The application must include the registered office address (a physical address in New Zealand, not a PO Box), the principal place of business, and the full names and addresses of all directors and shareholders. Payment of the filing fee (NZD 150) is made online. The Companies Office will review the application for completeness and compliance with the Companies Act 1993. Upon approval, a Certificate of Incorporation is issued electronically.
required_dossiers: Director and shareholder identification documents (passport, proof of address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the Companies Office will issue a notice specifying deficiencies. Correct the deficiencies and resubmit within 20 business days. If the application is suspended, file a formal response with supporting evidence to the Companies Office within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Inland Revenue Department (IRD), and other regulatory bodies as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, the company must immediately register for tax purposes with the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) to obtain an IRD number and GST registration if annual turnover exceeds NZD 60,000. The company must also file a 'Company Details' form with the Companies Office to confirm the appointment of directors and secretary. Additionally, the company must open a bank account in its name, providing the certificate of incorporation and director identification. The company must also appoint an auditor if required by the constitution or if the company is a large company as defined by the Companies Act 1993.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD registration is delayed, contact the IRD business helpline and provide the certificate of incorporation. If the bank account application is rejected, provide additional due diligence documents or choose an alternative financial institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office, IRD, and the company's board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to adopt the pro-forma resolution (as provided above) and record minutes. Ensure that the company maintains a share register, a director's register, and a minute book. File the annual return with the Companies Office within 30 days of the anniversary of incorporation. Prepare and file financial statements with the IRD and, if required, with the Companies Office. Ensure compliance with the Companies Act 1993, including the maintenance of a registered office and the appointment of a company secretary (if required).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is not filed on time, a late filing penalty will be imposed. File immediately and pay the penalty. If the company fails to maintain proper records, the Companies Office may issue a compliance notice; rectify the deficiency within the specified period.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand, administered through the 'myIR' secure online portal at www.ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity obtains an IRD number (the single statutory tax identification number) by applying to Inland Revenue and submitting certified corporate documents; once the entity intends to carry on a taxable activity or makes taxable supplies in New Zealand, it registers for GST through myIR if the NZD 60,000 threshold is met or exceeded. Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, the IRD number is used for income tax, GST, PAYE, and withholding tax; no separate VAT identification number is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Eligible close-held companies may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) status under the Income Tax Act 2007; GST registration may be elected voluntarily; GST group members may elect to file as a single registered person under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. New Zealand does not have a US-style check-the-box election, and hybrid mismatch rules apply automatically rather than by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in a rolling 12-month period; non-resident suppliers of remote services (including programmatic advertising/SSP services) also register when taxable remote supplies to New Zealand consumers exceed NZD 60,000 in 12 months
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping is required in New Zealand. E-invoicing is optional and operates through the PEPPOL network; New Zealand government agencies are required to accept PEPPOL-compatible e-invoices. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR, and registration details are maintained by Inland Revenue.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under section 11(1) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 for goods physically exported from New Zealand and for services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not connected to New Zealand land or goods and are not supplied to a New Zealand fixed establishment of the recipient. For goods, physical export must occur within the 28-day statutory export window. For the programme advertising/SSP model, the supplier must retain current documentary evidence of the recipient's non-resident status and the offshore receipt of consideration; for services, no physical customs cycle applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Electronic Export Declaration lodged through the Trade Single Window for physical exports
Ocean bill of lading or airway bill evidencing actual export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the goods and overseas destination
SWIFT/MT103 foreign exchange receipt confirmation or bank inward remittance advice evidencing payment from the non-resident buyer
For zero-rated services: executed customer contract, nature of services statement, and a certificate of tax residence or foreign business registration extract for the non-resident recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reassess a supply at the standard 15% GST rate if the documentary export file is incomplete, if goods do not leave New Zealand within the 28-day statutory export period, or if the non-resident status of the recipient is not established. Clawback assessments may include use-of-money interest; shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 range from 20% for an unacceptable tax position up to 150% for evasion, with criminal prosecution available for fraudulent export zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) acting as the central bank and prudential supervisor, with external exchange control functions managed under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a free-floating exchange rate regime with full and unrestricted convertibility of the New Zealand dollar (NZD) across both current account and capital account transactions. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not impose exchange control regulations, mandatory surrender requirements, or prior approval mechanisms for foreign currency transactions. There are no restrictions on the repatriation of dividends, capital, or loan repayments for non-resident investors, provided corporate governance formalities such as director resolutions and Inland Revenue compliance are observed. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 does impose screening on certain sensitive land and commercial fishing assets, but standard operational activities in the programmatic advertising technology sector are not notifiable. Trade settlement, service payments for real-time media procurement, and intercompany funding can flow freely through the banking system without FX licensing. Profit remittance is subject only to standard taxation obligations, including Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on dividends and interest, which can be reduced under New Zealand's double tax agreements. Overall, New Zealand is a fully liberalized capital account jurisdiction with no surrender, conversion quota, or waiting-period impediments, making it a highly efficient liquidity hub for cross-border treasury operations in the AdTech and digital advertising value chain.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign currency receipts. Exporters of services, including programmatic advertising and SSP platform fees, may retain all foreign currency earnings in multi-currency accounts or convert them to NZD at their discretion without any surrender obligation to the Reserve Bank or any authorized dealer.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (NZD and multi-currency)
Capital Escrow Account and Non-Resident Operative Account
Corporate Cash Management Account with SWIFT connectivity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise Business, Revolut Business, and similar payment service providers have moderate-to-high feasibility only as ancillary settlement rails for low-value programmatic payouts within New Zealand. However, they are not licensed as registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act and are therefore legally barred from taking deposits or issuing NZD account numbers that participate in the domestic Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) and BECS clearing. Offshore EMIs also lack the statutory capacity to hold capital escrow funds, issue official NZD bank confirmation letters for capital verification, or support the International Investment Position reporting obligations to Statistics New Zealand. Consequently, for the NZ_LTD treasury blueprint, offshore digital EMIs should be used exclusively for merchant payouts and small-volume publisher disbursements, while all capital injection, tax settlement, and major trade settlement flows must be routed through a Tier-1 domestic registered commercial bank to ensure full prudential compliance and auditability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Standard onboarding for a non-resident-owned New Zealand limited company requires the statutory directors and all ultimate beneficial owners to complete bank-mandated identity verification. Most Tier-1 New Zealand banks require at least one director or UBO holding significant control to appear either physically in-branch at a New Zealand commercial banking location or via a bank-authorised remote video conference authenticated by a compliance officer. Where physical appearance is impossible due to geopolitical or travel constraints, a consular proxy may be accepted if the director executes an affidavit, provides notarially certified passport copies, and engages the bank through a documented video call with embassy consular attestation. However, remote onboarding for a Low_Risk_Standard entity such as a programmatic AdTech SSP is becoming increasingly accepted, provided the bank Compliance Committee approves enhanced due diligence files, a third-party sanctions screening report, and certified corporate registry documents from the New Zealand Companies Office within 30 days of the original application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership opacity where non-resident shareholders or discretionary trust structures obscure the natural persons controlling the NZ limited company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Current and historical certificate of incorporation and company extract from the New Zealand Companies Office confirming all shareholders and directors; (2) an up-to-date UBO register naming every natural person holding 25% or more ownership or control; (3) the underlying trust deed and trustee appointment instrument if ownership routes through a trust; (4) statutory declarations from each UBO confirming source of wealth and source of funds; and (5) a corporate org-chart showing the full ownership chain to ultimate natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of Funds uncertainty for the initial capital injection and recurrent programmatic ad settlement flows where the volume of media transactions appears disproportionate to equity capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certified bank statements from the funding shareholder's institutional bank covering a continuous 12-month period; (2) an executed board resolution of NZ_LTD approving the capital injection and treasury mandate; (3) signed commercial contracts with advertisers, agencies, exchanges, and publishers evidencing the economic substance of the programmatic flow; (4) a rolling 12-month cash flow forecast and invoice trail matching all inbound settlement traffic; and (5) an independent accountant's letter confirming the funding is not derived from third-party pass-throughs or layering vehicles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or adverse media screening hits triggered by director nationalities, parent-country exposure, or prior corporate registry discrepancies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Valid biometric passports of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs; (2) independent sanctions and PEP screening reports from a global database such as Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, Refinitiv World-Check, or LexisNexis Bridger; (3) police clearance certificates from the country of residence for each director, issued within the previous six months; (4) a written narrative explanation addressing any screening hit or name-alias match with corroborating court judgments, disclaimers, or identity certificates; and (5) a resolution from the board confirming no individual is listed on any United Nations, OFAC, EU, or NZ jurisdiction-specific sanctions list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax identification and IRD number registry inconsistencies triggering Inland Revenue cross-checks and potential foreign tax avoidance red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certificate of IRD number registration issued by Inland Revenue New Zealand confirming the entity is an active tax resident; (2) confirmation of the entity's non-resident withholding tax classification and applicable DTA rate; (3) tax residence certificates from the home jurisdictions of all foreign shareholders to substantiate treaty eligibility; (4) an annual financial projection or accountant-prepared forecast proving the NZ entity will operate with real economic substance, local payroll, and ad-tech infrastructure rather than serving as a shell; and (5) a completed IRS/IRD entity classification form corroborating that the NZ_LTD is not a transparent or hybrid mismatch vehicle under OECD BEPS rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection for NZ_LTD must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's institutional bank to the NZ_LTD Tier-1 corporate account in New Zealand, using the IMF/OECD balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment and specifying the NZ IRD number in the payment reference. The remitting bank should state 'Equity Capital Subscription' as the transaction narrative. Upon credit, the receiving New Zealand bank issues a formal credit confirmation used by the company's auditor for capital verification, alongside a statutory declaration by the director and a Companies Office share-issue return. If a share premium is included, the purpose code should reference 'Share Premium Reserve' to ensure accurate classification. For cross-border inflows exceeding 10 million NZD annually, the entity must complete an International Investment Position return to Statistics New Zealand through the approved reporting portal, and the RBNZ may require monthly external asset and liability reporting for any financial intercompany account balances. All inbound capital must clear the New Zealand bank's sanctions screening and source-of-wealth profiling before settlement, and no portion of the capital injection may be denominated in cryptocurrencies unless a prior exemption from the Reserve Bank and FMA has been obtained.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements from NZ_LTD for programmatic AdTech trade settlements will employ four principal clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for all high-value publisher and supplier settlements through the correspondent international banking network, with explicit service purpose codes and invoice references to maintain audit integrity; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit governed by ICC UCP600 for any media inventory procurement or infrastructure hardware acquisition that demands a bank guarantee against documents; (iii) Documentary Collections governed by ICC URC522 for lower-trust remittance markets where shipping, licensing, or service acceptance documents must be exchanged through banks; and (iv) New Zealand BECS/ACH direct entry for domestic publisher payouts under 100,000 NZD where immediate finality is not required. Every outbound transfer is subject to bank AML screening, and payments to sanctioned or embargoed jurisdictions are automatically blocked. Outbound service fees to foreign advertising exchanges should be classified under the appropriate services code in the bank's FX schedules, and dividend or management-fee payments to non-resident parents will invoke Non-Resident Withholding Tax at the applicable DTA rate unless a certificate of exemption is filed with Inland Revenue.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (plain vanilla NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/AUD and NZD/GBP) with maturities up to 12 months, requiring no underlying documentary proof beyond a board-approved hedging policy
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) only for cross-currency exposures such as NZD/CNY or NZD/INR where the counterpart currency has onshore delivery constraints, although NZD itself is fully deliverable
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and interest rate coupled swaps) for intercompany loan principal and interest-repayment streams, subject to bank credit limits and master agreement execution
Vanilla FX options (call and put with standard New York/European physical delivery conventions) for seasonal treasury protection, requiring pre-approved credit facility and no speculative purpose

Forward rate agreements and rolling hedges on NZD reference rates used to stabilise operating cash flows from the programmatic auction clearing cycle, provided all positions comply with the Reserve Bank's non-bank counterparty credit standards

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a Limited Company (Companies Act 1993, s 213)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: file within 20 working days after the company's annual return date, which is the anniversary of incorporation. The official reminder specifies the exact date in each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file constitutes an offence; the Registrar may issue a default notice and, after continued non-compliance across three consecutive annual return periods, may publish a notice and remove/strike the company off the New Zealand Register under ss 318(1)(d) and 320 of the Companies Act 1993. Directors and officers are liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding NZD 10,000 (approximately USD 6,000), and the entity loses legal capacity to carry on business until reinstatement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake), New Zealand Government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, file by 7 July immediately following the tax year. Approved substituted balance dates are allowed; tax-agent extensions are available and may push the filing date to 28 February / 31 March in certain cases.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers automatic late filing penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 (currently NZD 250 per event and escalating monthly penalties for continued default), plus use-of-money interest on any unpaid terminal or provisional tax. Failure to furnish a return can lead to civil penalties up to NZD 25,000 and, for serious evasion, criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and Services Tax (GST) Return if registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - GST Registration and Filing (Te Tari Taake)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Periodic, not annual: due no later than 28 days after the end of each GST period (normally monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly). A company with turnover above NZD 60,000 (approx USD 36,000) is required to register and file accordingly.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and late-payment penalties apply under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and Tax Administration Act 1994, including a late filing penalty, a late payment penalty of up to 1% per month on unpaid GST, and use-of-money interest; continued refusal to file may result in IRD assessment by estimation and collection enforcement, including statutory demand and liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Financial Statements and Auditor's Report, if a compulsory audit threshold is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (filed under the Financial Reporting Act 2013) and, if FMC reporting entity, the Financial Markets Authority (FMA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after balance date for the financial statements and signed auditor's report; listed issuers and FMC reporting entities have the shorter timeframes imposed by FMC Act 2013 / NZX Listing Rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare or file audited financial statements may be prosecuted under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; penalties include fines up to NZD 50,000 for the entity and directors, a further daily fine for continuing default, and the Registrar may move to remove the company from the register for persistent default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A standard NZ private limited company must appoint a licensed statutory auditor (Chartered Accountant/CPA holding a Certificate of Public Practice) when it is (i) an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, including a listed issuer, registered bank, licensed insurer, manager of a registered scheme, or similar public-interest entity; (ii) a 'large company' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, namely, for each of the two preceding accounting periods, total consolidated assets exceed NZD 30,000,000 (approx USD 18,000,000) at balance date or annual consolidated total operating revenue exceeds NZD 60,000,000 (approx USD 36,000,000); or (iii) an audit is otherwise directed by shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights, by the Court, or required by a relevant sector regulator. Merely having a headcount above 25 FTE is not a standalone statutory audit trigger for an ordinary AdTech advertising-technology exchange/supply-side-platform company; employee-count tests apply only in regulated sectors or specific AML/CFT and tax-group reporting contexts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1 for-profit reporting entities; Tier 2 entities are entitled to apply NZ IFRS with the Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR); small/medium non-reporting entities may apply the XRB-approved Simplified Financial Reporting (SMP) framework or special-purpose reporting where no statutory general purpose financial reporting obligation exists. All statutory financial statements must still be true and fair and comply with the Companies Act 1993 and Financial Reporting Act 2013, with tax-basis adjustments reported separately to Inland Revenue.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no separate annual UBO confirmation return on the register. The mandatory annual return to the Companies Office is the statutory confirmation point at which the company confirms its current directors, shareholders, registered office, and addresses. Share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members within 10 working days of registration; returns of allotment for newly issued shares must be delivered to the Registrar within 10 working days after allotment. There is no 30-day reporting window for share transfers to the register; the 10-working-day Companies Act timeline governs, and the annual return then repeats that information as at the anniversary date. If the AdTech platform itself becomes an AML/CFT reporting entity by offering financial products or banking-style payment services, ongoing beneficial-owner identification, verification, risk rating, and record-keeping must be maintained under the AML/CFT Act 2009, but an ordinary advertising DSP/SSP is not an AML/CFT reporting entity solely because it uses ACH/SWIFT to move receipts.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including share transfers and ultimate registered shareholding)
Register of Directors (including addresses and changes)
Register of Charges/Mortgages (all security interests granted by the company)
Minute Book (minutes of shareholder and board meetings and resolutions)
Register of Share Certificate and Transfer Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 30,000 per annum for a private NZ limited AdTech vehicle, depending on consolidated turnover, transaction volume, group structure, and NZ IFRS audit scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand has no patent box and no preferential free-zone corporate tax regime; the headline 28% corporate rate applies. The principal statutory incentive is the R&D Tax Incentive, a refundable tax credit of 15% on qualifying R&D expenditure above NZD 50,000 up to a NZD 120 million cap, which for a programmatic AdTech SSP/DSP business can reduce the effective rate on qualifying software/algorithm development. Imputation credits avoid double taxation on distributed dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR portal; supporting financial statements are supplied on IR10 when required by IRD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the 7th day of the fourth month following the balance date; for the standard 31 March balance date, filing is due by 7 July. Tax agents may receive an extended filing date through IRD's standard due date regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income/turnover from programmatic advertising, ad-exchange fees, SSP platform services, DSP demand-side fees and associated technical services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: As a New Zealand resident company, worldwide income is taxable. Report all gross consideration recognized under the accounting revenue standard, irrespective of the foreign advertiser or publisher location. Do not net intercompany platform fees or enter a reduced amount based on alleged offshore performance unless a contemporaneous transfer pricing analysis supports the split and New Zealand has no Permanent Establishment exposure from the foreign functions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest, dividends and other investment income, including foreign-sourced passive income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose passive income separately. Dividends received from non-resident subsidiaries must be tested under the Controlled Foreign Company and Foreign Investment Fund rules; foreign income tax credits must be evidenced by foreign tax records. Cross-border interest and royalty receipts from a non-resident client may be New Zealand-sourced and subject to allocation rules where the payer uses the right in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses, including intercompany management fees, data licensing, cloud infrastructure, advertising inventory costs, user acquisition and third-party technology fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid or payable to non-residents must satisfy economic substance and arm's length rules. Intercompany service charges require proof of actual provision, benefit, and no duplication; payments for the use of intellectual property may be recharacterized as royalties and are New Zealand-sourced if used in New Zealand. Add back non-deductible entertainment expenditure and any payments subject to concurrent NRWT obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing adjustments increasing or decreasing taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the intercompany transaction price departs from arm's length, enter an adjustment under Income Tax Act 2007 s GC 13. For a NZ Ltd with non-resident ownership, thin capitalization rules apply if debt exceeds 60% of gross assets; excess interest deductions are disallowed and must be added back. A common fatal error is claiming a related-party expense in Box 3 and then reducing Box 4 without an IRD-compliant adjustment schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: imputation credits, resident withholding tax credits, foreign income tax credits, and the R&D Tax Incentive credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach valid dividend statements, RWT certificates and foreign tax evidence. Tax credits cannot be used to satisfy NRWT that should have been withheld from outbound dividends, interest or royalties because NRWT is a final tax liability of the non-resident recipient, collected at the NZ payor level. A non-resident shareholder cannot claim imputation credit refunds except under specific DTA provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating losses carried forward and utilized in the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A NZ company may carry forward a tax loss only if the 49% shareholder continuity requirement is satisfied throughout the continuity period, or where the same business test applies. For a wholly non-resident owned NZ Ltd, any change in the ultimate beneficial ownership chain must be tracked; the loss claim is disallowed if continuity is broken. Losses do not offset the income of other group entities absent a written tax loss grouping election under Part IG of the Income Tax Act 2007.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident and DTA beneficial ownership schedule, including directors' certification of the residence and substance of all foreign related-party recipients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare whether each shareholder, lender, or licensor is a tax resident of a DTA partner country. For treaty reduction, the NZ payor must hold a valid foreign Tax Residency Certificate and a beneficial ownership declaration from the recipient. If a recipient is a conduit or lacks economic substance, the DTA benefit is denied and full statutory NRWT applies; an offshore parent that is merely an invoice pass-through may also trigger a permanent establishment in the ultimate market.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D Tax Incentive claim for eligible software, algorithms, and platform development activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Eligible R&D must involve systematic investigation, pilot activity or resolving technological uncertainty. For an AdTech platform, covered costs may include developer wages, cloud testing, and data-science experimentation; prohibited items include advertising spend, routine hosting, and user acquisition. Provide the required IRD supplementary schedule; the credit is refundable to the extent of NZD 50,000 minimum adjusted taxable loss, but not against NRWT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable calculation: net corporate income at 28%, terminal tax and provisional tax reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company has cross-border receipts, ensure that payments to a non-resident for services rendered outside New Zealand are not incorrectly included as NZ-sourced income; conversely, income from programmatic data or DSP/SSP software exploited in New Zealand is sourced to New Zealand. Payment of the assessed tax must accompany the return on or before the due date; late payment triggers immediate penalties before any filing extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director's declaration: correctness of the return, completeness of records, and compliance with transfer pricing and NRWT obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A director must personally attest that the books and records are complete, that intercompany prices reflect the arm's length standard, that documentary evidence supports all travel/entertainment claims, and that no undisclosed offshore accounts or nominee shareholdings exist. A false declaration knowingly made is the basis for criminal prosecution for tax evasion and for piercing the corporate veil to impose personal liability on the director.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of IR4 attracts an initial late filing penalty of NZD 250 plus a further NZD 250 for each subsequent six months; late payment penalties are 1% immediately on the due date and a further 4% after seven days, with use-of-money interest accruing daily. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 Part IX range from 20% for lack of reasonable care to 40% for an unsubstantiated tax position and 50% for an abusive tax position; evasion or similar acts attract a penalty of up to 150% of the shortfall. Criminal liability may include fines up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment under Crimes Act 1961 s 228, and a false IR4 return can trigger director disqualification.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Within New Zealand, the statutory Non-Resident Withholding Tax rate on gross dividends paid by a NZ company to a non-resident shareholder is 30%. The tax is final, is withheld at source by the paying company, and attaches to the full amount of the dividend before the application of any Double Tax Agreement rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident recipient must provide the New Zealand payor with a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its home jurisdiction tax authority, complete the Inland Revenue reduced-rate NRWT certificate/notification, and give a written beneficial ownership undertaking. The payor must retain the TRC and the undertaking in the company's tax records. In addition, the recipient must not be a conduit or a contractually obliged pass-through to a resident of a third country. Under OECD standards, a substance company must itself conduct the economic business and bear the risks to qualify as beneficial owner; absent documentary substantiation, the NZ payor must withhold the full statutory 30% on dividends, 15% on interest and 15% on royalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For outbound interest, the statutory NRWT rate is 15%; the 2% Approved Issuer Levy may apply to eligible interest if the loan arrangement is publicly issued debt, but the general cross-border statutory rate for intercompany debt is 15%. For outbound royalties, the statutory NRWT rate is 15%. Under the New Zealand-United States DTA, interest may be reduced to 10% and royalties to 5%; under the New Zealand-Australia DTA, interest is commonly capped at 10% and royalties at 5%, generally where the recipient that is associated with the payor is resident in the treaty partner and satisfies beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10 million aggregate cross-border related-party transactions is the generally accepted threshold recognized by the IRD in its transfer pricing operational statement for contemporaneous Local File / Master File preparation; separate Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory for New Zealand-resident MNE groups with consolidated group revenue above EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulation regime, but the IRD applies OECD BEPS principles and tax avoidance doctrines to strip benefits from shell structures. For a NZ Ltd operating a programmatic AdTech platform, Core Income-Generating Activities include real-time bid- and ad-inventory decisioning, contract negotiation with DSP/SSP partners, platform risk management, data stewardship, and treasury management. If some or all of these functions are actually performed outside New Zealand through a paper offshore entity, the NZ entity may have a permanent establishment in that offshore jurisdiction; conversely, a foreign interposed company with no substance will not be recognized as beneficial owner for treaty purposes and profits will be re-attributed to New Zealand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The directors of the NZ Ltd divert programmatic advertising and SSP/DSP platform revenue to a secret nominee bank account in Hong Kong or Singapore, omit the remittances from IR4, and create false deduction invoices for data intelligence services with no personnel or operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: This constitutes evasion under the Tax Administration Act 1994, attracting a shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the evaded tax, use-of-money interest, late payment penalties and criminal sanctions. Under s 144 TAA 1994 and s 228 Crimes Act 1961, a person who intentionally obtains a tax advantage by deceit is liable to imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced because the evasion is a deliberate wrongdoing: directors are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the evaded tax plus penalties, may face charges of dishonest use of corporate documents, may be disqualified as directors, barred from leaving New Zealand under a Departure Prohibition Order, and sentenced to terms of imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ Ltd is registered with no office, no employees, no real platform operations, and no bank account in New Zealand; it is used solely as an invoicing shell to route programmatic ad inventory through a low-tax jurisdiction and to claim DTA benefits on outbound dividends or royalties from a parent entity that is a pure conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The arrangement is void against the Commissioner under Income Tax Act 2007 ss BG 1 and GB 1 as a tax avoidance arrangement; transfer pricing adjustments are imposed under s GC 13; the tax shortfall penalty is increased to 40-50% for the abusive tax position, and treaty benefits are denied under the DTA Limitation on Benefits / Principal Purpose Test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement a sham may be personally liable for amounts unpaid by the company under the intentional wrongdoing exceptions; they face civil restitution, insolvent trading liability under Companies Act 1995 s 135, disqualification under s 383, travel restrictions and criminal imprisonment when the sham is used to defraud revenue authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) Evasion and False DTA Certification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company pays dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident related party without deducting NRWT, or obtains a reduced DTA rate by submitting a fake Tax Residency Certificate and false beneficial ownership declarations for an interposed entity lacking substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s 149 Tax Administration Act 1994, unpaid RWT/NRWT can be recovered jointly and severally from directors; the failure to withhold and the knowingly false treaty document constitute an abusive tax position attracting up to 50% shortfall penalty, further late payment penalties, use-of-money interest, and a criminal evasion fine of up to NZD 50,000 plus imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for non-payment of withholding taxes: directors and shadow directors are personally liable for the unpaid NRWT, civil asset restitution may be ordered, the director may be blacklisted and prohibited from departing New Zealand, and imprisonment may follow where the false certification was made knowingly.
